content.title: About
content.content: Soy yogurt is a fermented beverage made from soy milk. It has a creamy texture, a mildly tangy flavor, and is often fortified with vitamins and minerals to match the nutritional profile of traditional dairy yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy yogurt is suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance.
It is frequently fortified with calcium and vitamin D to compensate for the lower natural levels in soy milk.
Soy products contain isoflavones, which may have beneficial effects on hormonal balance.
Unlike dairy yogurt, soy yogurt typically contains no cholesterol.
Manufacturers often add probiotic strains such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium to support gut health.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of soy yogurt provides about 6–8 g of protein, useful for maintaining muscle mass.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Fortified soy yogurt can deliver up to 30 % of the daily calcium requirement, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in sugar (when unsweetened)
items.content: Plain soy yogurt contains little sugar, making it suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Contains isoflavones
items.content: Soy isoflavones may support heart health and act as antioxidants.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Probiotics in the yogurt help balance intestinal flora and improve digestive function.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy may experience reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis when consuming soy yogurt.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Soy contains phytic acid, which can reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in excess.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Some brands sweeten their soy yogurt, increasing calorie content and glycemic impact.

items.title: GMO concerns
items.content: Much of the commercial soy supply is genetically modified; choose non‑GMO labeled products if this matters to you.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soy yogurt can be enjoyed on its own, blended into smoothies, mixed with granola, fruit salads, or used as a base for sauces and desserts. Sweeten with honey, maple syrup, or fresh berries if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soy yogurt in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days and do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
